nodes.title: Bounded sequences
nodes.text: A bounded sequence stays inside a fixed finite interval.

nodes.title: Subsequences
nodes.text: A subsequence selects terms while preserving their original order.

nodes.title: Convergent examples
nodes.text: A sequence can have a convergent subsequence without converging itself.

nodes.title: Uniform continuity
nodes.text: A continuous function on a closed bounded interval is uniformly continuous.

nodes.title: Oscillation
nodes.text: Oscillation is the difference between the supremum and infimum on an interval.

nodes.title: Continuity exercise
nodes.text: Estimate the oscillation of a continuous function on a small interval.

nodes.title: Partitions
nodes.text: A partition divides an interval into finitely many adjacent pieces.

nodes.title: Step functions
nodes.text: A step function is constant on each piece of a finite partition.

nodes.title: Upper and lower sums
nodes.text: Use infima and suprema on each interval to form lower and upper sums.

nodes.title: Refinement lemma
nodes.text: Refining a partition raises the lower sum and lowers the upper sum.

nodes.title: Common refinement
nodes.text: Two partitions have a common refinement containing both sets of endpoints.

nodes.title: Integrability criterion
nodes.text: A bounded function is integrable when its upper and lower sums can be made arbitrarily close.

nodes.title: Continuous implies integrable
nodes.text: Every continuous function on a closed bounded interval is Riemann integrable.

nodes.title: A smooth curve
nodes.text: Refine rectangle approximations for a smooth curve on a closed interval.

nodes.title: Integrate a quadratic
nodes.text: Use regular partitions to integrate a quadratic from zero to one.

nodes.title: An oscillating example
nodes.text: Compare sums for the function equal to one on rational points and zero otherwise.

nodes.title: Compare two sums
nodes.text: Compare upper and lower approximations with four, eight, and sixteen intervals.

nodes.title: Further integral properties
nodes.text: Pointwise comparison of continuous functions gives a comparison of integrals.

nodes.title: Difference quotients
nodes.text: Measure the change in a function relative to the change in its input.

nodes.title: The derivative
nodes.text: A derivative is the limit of difference quotients when that limit exists.

nodes.title: Derivative of a square
nodes.text: Expand the numerator and cancel before taking the limit.

nodes.title: Product rule
nodes.text: Differentiate a product by splitting the change into two contributions.

nodes.title: Chain rule
nodes.text: Differentiate a composition by multiplying the two derivatives.

nodes.title: Composition exercise
nodes.text: Apply the chain rule to a trigonometric composition.

nodes.title: Mean value theorem
nodes.text: Some instantaneous slope equals the slope across a closed interval.

nodes.title: Monotonicity
nodes.text: A nonnegative derivative on an interval makes the function nondecreasing.

nodes.title: Pointwise convergence
nodes.text: At each input, the sequence of values converges separately.

nodes.title: A moving peak
nodes.text: A narrow moving peak distinguishes pointwise behavior from uniform behavior.

nodes.title: Uniform convergence
nodes.text: One bound on the error works over the entire domain.

nodes.title: Uniform Cauchy criterion
nodes.text: Uniform Cauchy control describes convergence without first knowing the limit.

nodes.title: Continuity of a limit
nodes.text: A uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous.

nodes.title: Integrating a limit
nodes.text: Uniform convergence on a compact interval permits exchanging limit and integral.

nodes.title: A uniform approximation
nodes.text: Estimate the integral error using the largest pointwise error.

nodes.title: Function series
nodes.text: Study a series of functions through its partial sums.

nodes.title: Uniform comparison
nodes.text: A summable sequence of uniform bounds controls the tails of a function series.

nodes.title: A geometric series
nodes.text: A geometric series converges uniformly on any closed interval strictly inside its radius.
